parsed.explanation: Combined national-state regime yields low-end Elevated Risk. National executive-order facility exclusion and visa/border screening (case-note tagging, refusal, possible fraud finding) are traveller-facing exposures; the state adds a school-ground birth-certificate restroom rule, removed gender-identity accommodations protections, and no local remedy. Custody/immigration detention abuse and official 'radically pro-transgender' threat framing raise severity if detained. Offsets are partial: no criminalisation of trans identity, national hate-crime coverage, state court adult care coverage, and no documented street sweeps or state violence data. Adult non-school facility access and enforcement against visitors remain uncertain.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas and stop X markers; a border cable tags cases, directs refusal where sex discrepancy or reasonable doubt exists, and flags possible permanent fraud ineligibility. Travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and regional advisories/detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the passport policy is under national court challenge; visitors ordinarily use their own foreign passports.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport or presentation mismatch can trigger secondary screening, visa refusal or fraud inquiry, feeding into detention exposure; state law offers no service/accommodation remedy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies impose conversion-therapy-like practices, hormone removal and care denial on trans inmates; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some executive orders are enjoined; no documented visitor-specific custody safeguard.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy can escalate to immigration detention, where abusive custody practices are documented; state-specific custody rules are not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; state school law requires everyone on school grounds, including visitors, to use restrooms/changing rooms by birth-certificate sex, with single-person option framed as student/guardian accommodation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented statewide adult public-restroom ban outside schools; private hotels are not shown barred; state courts have protected adult surgery coverage.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and school rules stack; an adult visitor is exposed in federal buildings and on school grounds; no state public-accommodations remedy if excluded.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for under-18s; national orders frame minor care as mutilation and propose insurance bars; national health agencies removed gender terms.
care_services.protection: State courts preserved adult gender-affirming surgery coverage; emergency-care exclusion is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Adult ordinary emergency care is not shown excluded; a travelling minor cannot access transition care, and official climate may deter disclosure to medics.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralization; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; state removed gender-identity civil-rights protections and barred stronger local ordinances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; courts have enjoined some orders; no state remedy for public-accommodation refusal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises risk around advocacy/visibility and discourages police recourse; ordinary tourist targeting is not documented, but state remedies are absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: State school restroom/changing rule binds all on school grounds, including visiting adults and minors; single-person alternative is only a student accommodation with guardian consent; under-18 gender-affirming care is banned.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented enforcement against visiting minors at school events beyond statutory wording; an adult guardian can accompany but cannot override the birth-certificate rule.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor at a school/campus event faces birth-cert facilities; a trans minor faces care ban and official hostility; enforcement against visitors is uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans violence data; state removed public-accommodations protection and has no gender-identity civil-rights remedy; national climate is hostile.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state courts have sometimes protected trans adults; no documented police sweeps/extortion in this state.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If refused service or assaulted, a visitor has no state accommodation remedy; a national hate-crime route exists, but state-level bias coverage is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State bars localities from stronger protections and removed gender identity from civil rights; a visitor refused service has no state-law remedy; passport/border rules remain contested.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National civil-liberties litigation challenges passport policy; state court adult care coverage; national hate-crime statute.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are uneven and contested; adult non-school facility access and enforcement of the school rule against visitors are not documented, so uncertainty is not treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable universal birth-sex facility exposure and no visitor exemption. This dossier adds border document/refusal risk and state removal of accommodations remedies, but lacks documented staff checks across all public buildings and court-rejected complaints. It sits near, but slightly above, the 0.35-A pattern.

Both have universal government-facility birth-sex rules and no organized street arrests. This dossier's state facility rule is narrower (school grounds only), but entry screening/tagging and official threat framing are additional exposures. Roughly similar to 0.45-A.

0.55-B has recurring hostile service treatment, but mediators secure readmissions/refunds and police convict. This dossier lacks a working service remedy and adds universal facility exclusion and border risk. Materially lower than 0.55-B.
0.75-C has traditional acceptance, facilities by identity and enforced compensation. This dossier has official hostile framing, facility restrictions and no state accommodations remedy. Much lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a stacked national-state system. National executive-order facility exclusion and border screening create traveller-facing exposure at entry and in federal single-sex facilities; the state adds a school-ground birth-certificate restroom rule, repealed gender-identity accommodations protections, and no local remedy. Detention/custody is the severest branch: border discrepancy can lead to immigration custody where abuse is documented. Official counterterrorism rhetoric intensifies threat framing. Offsets are partial: no criminalisation of trans identity, national hate-crime coverage, state court protection for adult care, and no documented street sweeps or state-specific violence rate. Because universal facility and border exposures lack a working visitor remedy, the combined regime sits at the low end of Elevated Risk.
